English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian duetto.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Rhymes: -ɛtəʊ

Noun

[edit]

duetto (plural duettos or duettoes)

  1. Archaic form of duet.

References

[edit]
  • “duetto”, in Webster’s Revised Unabridged Dictionary, Springfield, Mass.: G. & C. Merriam, 1913, →OCLC.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • touted

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian duetto.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈduetːo/, [ˈdue̞t̪ːo̞]
  • Rhymes: -uetːo
  • Syllabification(key): du‧et‧to
  • Hyphenation(key): du‧et‧to

Noun

[edit]

duetto

  1. duet (a musical composition for two performers)

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian duetto.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /dɥɛ.to/ ~ /dɥe.to/

Noun

[edit]

duetto m (plural duettos)

  1. (music) a duet

Further reading

[edit]
  • “duetto”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Italian

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From due +‎ -etto (diminutive). Cognate with Piedmontese duèt.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /duˈet.to/
  • Rhymes: -etto
  • Hyphenation: du‧ét‧to

Noun

[edit]

duetto m (plural duetti)

  1. (music) duet
  2. duo
Derived terms
[edit]
  • duettare
Related terms
[edit]
  • due
Descendants
[edit]
  • → English: duet, duetto
  • → Finnish: duetto
  • → French: duetto
  • → German: Duett
    • → Belarusian: дуэ́т (duét)
    • → Russian: дуэ́т (duét)
    • → Ukrainian: дуе́т (duét)

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

duetto

  1. first-person singular present indicative of duettare
